title: India's fireworks town made no fireworks 100 years ago
loop: Last line rhymes with the first

beats.say: Nearly every firework in India comes from one town. And a hundred years ago, that town made none.
beats.caption: Sivakasi · 100 years ago: none
beats.visual: Night sky bursts, then goes dark over a map pin

beats.say: Sivakasi, far south in Tamil Nadu. In nineteen twenty-two, two young men take a train to Calcutta. Not to learn fireworks. To learn how to make a matchbox.
beats.caption: 1922 · Calcutta · a matchbox
beats.visual: Rail line draws north-east; matchbox icon

beats.say: They come home with German machines and open a match factory. Then, to stand out, they add colour: sticks that burn red and green. Bengal lights.
beats.caption: 1923 · Bengal lights
beats.visual: Match strikes; flame turns red then green

beats.say: In nineteen thirty-eight, the town opens its first factory made only for fireworks.
beats.caption: 1938 · first fireworks factory

beats.say: Then the Second World War cuts off fireworks from abroad. The few licensed makers here get the whole market.
beats.caption: WWII · licences
beats.visual: Sea routes close; three factory icons

beats.say: India's biggest fireworks town didn't inherit a tradition. It copied a matchbox. And a hundred years ago, it made none.
beats.caption: Not tradition. A matchbox.
beats.visual: One lit match, held; cut to black

title: Why a fireworks town owns a printing press
gates: C016, C021 must clear (C021 only as 'the presses keep running')

beats.say: Why does a fireworks town own a printing press?
beats.caption: WHY A PRESS?
beats.visual: A press beside a firework factory

beats.say: Sivakasi, nineteen thirty-eight. Every matchbox and every cracker packet needs a bright paper label. And those labels come from presses in Bombay.
beats.caption: 1938 · labels from Bombay

beats.say: Slow, and costly. So K. S. A. Arunagiri Nadar sets up a printing press in Sivakasi itself.
beats.caption: National Litho Press

beats.say: Then the town notices something. When the fireworks season ends, the presses can keep running. Calendars. Diaries. Notebooks.
beats.caption: Calendars · diaries · notebooks

beats.say: That's why a fireworks town has a printing press. It never has a quiet season.
beats.caption: No quiet season
beats.visual: Press and sparkler side by side

title: 'Green' crackers are not pollution-free
gates: C022, C023, C025 must clear; the 30% figure needs a CSIR-NEERI source
loop: Last line rhymes with the first

beats.say: A green cracker is not a clean cracker.
beats.caption: Green ≠ clean

beats.say: In October twenty-eighteen, India's Supreme Court banned crackers made with barium salts. Sivakasi's makers needed a new recipe.
beats.caption: Oct 2018 · ban

beats.say: A government lab, CSIR-NEERI, developed green crackers. The lab's own claim: about a third less particle pollution. Not zero.
beats.caption: ~30% less. Not zero.

beats.say: How? The mix releases water vapour as it burns, which helps the dust settle. Picture a tiny mist sprayer inside the shell.
beats.caption: Water vapour settles dust

beats.say: So green doesn't mean clean. It means less.
beats.caption: Less. Not none.
